title: Rendered policies
description: The rendered policies, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #80: one segment contract rendered to N fabrics. The fabrics array declares the N — every well-formed contract rule must appear once per fabric — and each render row cites the contract rule it renders with the direction, type, and port it rendered, inside the modeled subset. The gate verifies the joins both ways: a rule missing from one render drifts silently (render/rule-missing), and a render carrying a rule the contract never had drifts just as silently (render/rule-unknown). This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/segment); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — fabrics declared and unique, render rows well-formed, every contract rule rendered on every declared fabric exactly once, and the direction, type, and port agreeing with the contract.

version.description: Version of the renders. The renders are versioned like the contract they render — rendered policies that nobody re-reads are rendered policies nobody still believes.

reviewedOn.description: Date the renders were last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

fabrics.description: The fabrics the renders cover — the N in one contract, N fabrics. A rule is not enforced until every fabric says so; a fabric declared twice is a render the gate cannot count.

rules.description: The render rows: one per contract rule per fabric. The gate flags a row citing a fabric the document never declared (render/fabric-undeclared), a rule the contract never declared (render/rule-unknown), the same rule rendered twice on one fabric (render/rule-duplicate), and direction, type, or port disagreements with the contract (render/direction-mismatch, render/type-mismatch, render/port-mismatch).

fabric.description: The fabric this row renders onto, e.g. cloud or host-firewall. Must be declared in fabrics.

rule.description: The contract rule this row renders, by id. A render carrying a rule the contract never had drifts silently — the gate cites both documents.

direction.description: The direction as rendered. Must agree with the contract within the modeled subset.

type.description: The protocol as rendered. Must agree with the contract within the modeled subset.

port.description: The port as rendered. Must agree with the contract.
